verses.1: The LORD said to Abram, "Leave your country, your people, and your father's household and go to the land I will show you.
verses.2: I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be a blessing.
verses.3: I will bless those who bless you, and whoever dishonors you I will curse, and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you."
verses.4: So Abram went, as the LORD had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
verses.5: Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all their possessions they had gathered, and the people they had acquired in Haran, and they set out for the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,
verses.6: Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.
verses.7: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "To your offspring I will give this land." So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
verses.8: From there he moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.
verses.9: Then Abram set out and continued toward the Negeb.
verses.10: Now there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to stay there for a while, because the famine was severe.
verses.11: As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "I know that you are a beautiful woman.
verses.12: When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will kill me but let you live.
verses.13: Say you are my sister, so that things will go well for me because of you and my life will be spared for your sake."
verses.14: When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful.
verses.15: When Pharaoh's officials saw her, they praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into Pharaoh's household.
verses.16: Because of her, Pharaoh treated Abram well, and Abram acquired sheep, cattle, male and female donkeys, male and female servants, and camels.
verses.17: But the LORD afflicted Pharaoh and his household with serious diseases because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
verses.18: So Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why did you not tell me she was your wife?
verses.19: Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her as my wife? Now here is your wife — take her and go."
verses.20: Then Pharaoh gave his men orders concerning Abram, and they sent him on his way with his wife and everything he had.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
